# Agent Browser — Browser Automation CLI for AI Agents

Curated by Skill Harbor — a fast browser-automation CLI built for AI agents: it drives Chrome/Chromium over CDP with accessibility-tree snapshots and compact element refs, so an agent can navigate pages, click buttons, fill forms, take screenshots, extract data, test web apps, or automate Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma) and Slack workspaces. Ships as a native Rust binary (no Playwright/Puppeteer dependency), with sessions, an authentication vault, state persistence and video recording; specialized skill packs load on demand (`electron`, `slack`, `dogfood` for exploratory QA, `vercel-sandbox`, `agentcore`). Discovered via skills.sh, listed here with credit to its creator by @vercel-labs. Honest caveats: this is a developer CLI, not an in-chat skill — install via `npm i -g agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install` for the browser; the SKILL.md in the repo is a discovery stub, the real usage content is served by the CLI itself (`agent-browser skills get core`) and always matches the installed version; most useful through an agent with computer access (like Muse) that can run the CLI for you. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
